report_review.scope_depth_review: Within the 1,300–1,700-word budget. The report compares four fan-in strategies across sparse/dense frontiers and weak/strong destination skew, distinguishes graph discovery from floating-point sum semantics, and includes local aggregation, segmented reduction, deterministic-order limits, counterexamples, and one discriminating experiment. Its claims remain literature hypotheses, not a local implementation recommendation or Arc performance claim.

It centers destination contention, duplicate keys, reduction order, and determinism. These distinctions were checked against R780 metadata rather than by reopening prior collection report bodies.

next_research_scopes.title: Diagnosing precision drift in long-sequence mixed-precision inference
next_research_scopes.finite_question: For deep residual and recurrent sequence-model inference, compare methods for detecting and localizing precision drift: per-layer activation error distributions and outliers, teacher-forced logit divergence and NLL, persistent-state trajectory drift, and end-task outcomes. When can a local tensor metric miss a downstream decision change, and when can a visible tensor error leave predictions unchanged? Separate storage-rounding effects from local FP32 accumulation, and identify the limits of teacher-forced versus generated-token comparisons. Do not survey mitigation methods or recommend a Strata precision change.
next_research_scopes.breadth_and_counterevidence: Use primary papers and framework/evaluation documentation. Compare local tensor, sequence-output, and task-level evidence, including cases where these indicators disagree. Keep the scope on diagnosis and metric interpretation; do not repeat R782's producer/consumer type contracts, R783's GEMM/API alternatives, or R785's conditional mitigation choices after a measured regression. Do not claim Strata quality, set an acceptance threshold, or infer Arc performance.
next_research_scopes.report_budget: 1,300–1,700 words; at most six substantive primary sources with exact URLs, one metric-comparison table, and one bounded prospective evaluation protocol.
next_research_scopes.prerequisites: Public source access only; no local quality result, device measurement, or implementation decision is required for a metric-method comparison.
prerequisite_evidence: AGENTS.md requires numerical/performance gates and preservation of the FP32 reference for current native-16 precision work.
The current research index records native16_activation_pipeline.quality_acceptance as UNSET and performance_qualified as false; Main confirms native16 quality and performance are not qualified.

R782 and R783 cover type/state boundaries and kernel/API choices; R785's precision-quality follow-up is conditional on a measured regression and concerns mitigation choices. The proposed measurement-localization question is distinct and does not depend on that regression.
next_research_scopes.novelty_guard: Limit the report to how evidence localizes or fails to localize numerical drift. Exclude error-feedback, rounding-policy, precision-allocation, and kernel-layout recommendations, which belong to other scopes or a later decision.
